statement-book.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity flat browser dashboard screenshot, 1440x900 landscape, no device frame. Product Ledgerly: read-only billing inspection in Rails. Operate mode, precise and quiet, Geist sans-serif, Geist Mono small IDs, pale blue-gray #f2f4f7 ground, white surfaces, ink #141414, muted #60646c, 1px #e4e7eb rules, small 6px corners, a tiny blue #1d5fbf accent only in data. No gradients, shadows, illustrations, marketing hero, charts without data, fake financial growth, icon tiles, or oversized type. Actual local counts: Customers 3, Usage events 3, Invoices 3, Webhooks 12, Ledger entries 24. USD ledger total debits 6.30, credits 6.30, difference 0.00. All 12 webhooks processed. Use anonymous row names 'Customer 1', 'Customer 2', 'Customer 3', INV-000001, INV-000002, INV-000003; amount labels 'USD', not dollar symbols. Row details are illustrative mockup placeholders and should have a small 'Layout preview' label. Fixed 256px sidebar with Ledgerly brand and small ledger mark, workspace 'Local test workspace', Stripe test mode; navigation Overview, Customers, Usage, Invoices, Ledger entries, Webhooks; bottom 'Read-only workspace', 'Sign out'. Main header 24px Overview, short 'A clear view of recorded billing activity.', Refresh button and UTC timestamp. All five data areas discoverable in first 900px. Exact legible text and careful right-aligned tabular amounts. Layout A: Statement book. Main top horizontal four-count strip, then full-width compact ledger double-entry book with separate Currency, Debits, Credits, Difference columns. Under it, two equal columns Recent invoices and Webhook activity with three compact rows each. Below that, two equal columns Customers and Latest usage with three rows each. Airy 24px margins, 12px panel gaps. This ledger book is the single visual anchor.
